result.title: Exact Fusion of Softmax Attention Heads Can Require Exponentially Many Atoms
result.comment: 9 pages, 3 figures. Code and reproducibility materials: https://github.com/usamihiroyasu/attention-head-fusion
result.summary: Fusing independently normalized attention heads can increase the number of explicit key-value entries, or atoms, needed to preserve their output. We prove a sharp separation for $W_d(q)=\sum_{j=1}^dσ(q_j)$: its $d$ two-atom heads use $2d$ head-atom terms, whereas its minimum single-head representation has exactly $2^d$ atoms, even with arbitrary fixed replacement keys, scalar values, and positive masses. The same lower bound holds for every fixed uniform error below $1/2$ on $\mathbb R^d$, and the threshold is sharp. The proof uses exposed-key normal cones; exact equality on any nonempty open query domain inherits the bound. The resulting atom bound for a fixed head count is tight when that count divides $d$. A normalized family retains its exponential exact minimum while approaching a constant on fixed-radius query balls. For pretrained-model caches, a classical affine-rank bound and a certified instance exclude exact vector preservation at a specified atom count. Learned-cache comparisons on two disjoint banks of 64 contexts show budget-dependent reversals and calibration effects.

AI.brief_summary: 论文证明把各自独立归一化的 softmax 多头注意力融合为单一表示时，保持输出所需的 key-value 原子数会从 2d 涨到恰好 2^d，并给出对任意固定键值、标量值下的指数下界、误差阈值与预训练模型缓存上的数值核查。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽不涉及视觉推理，但其「融合注意力头/缓存条目所需原子数」的容量下界可供核查 LVR 中把多头证据压缩成单一 latent 状态时的信息坍缩风险，以及与缓存预算相关的结构限制。
